codeReview.summary: Receipt entitlement and lifecycle-specific messaging are covered, and deprecated guest/public thank-you aliases are exercised. However, this feature did not add deterministic coverage for the restaurant thank-you alias even though the contract requires restaurant thank-you aliases to stay on one canonical route.

issues.description: The feature contract includes keeping restaurant thank-you aliases on one canonical route, but this feature's diff and added tests only cover public booking and guest thank-you redirects plus receipt messaging. The restaurant alias implementation existed already and remained unverified here, so the feature does not fully satisfy its assigned contract on its own.

sharedStateObservations.observation: The mission library documents `/restaurants/[slug]/thank-you` canonicalization, but there was no dedicated scrutiny evidence tied to this feature until a later follow-up feature covered it. That gap made it easy for this worker to mark the feature complete without proving the restaurant alias behavior required by the contract.
sharedStateObservations.evidence: .factory/library/guest-routes.md lists `/restaurants/[slug]/thank-you` as canonicalizing to `/restaurants/[slug]/book/thank-you`, while commit `98fc48a7` only changed `ReceiptClient.tsx`, `tests/guest/guest-receipt-pages.test.tsx`, and `tests/e2e/guest-receipt-pages.spec.ts`.

summary: Reviewed handoff, commit `98fc48a7`, transcript skeleton, mission guidance, and shared-state docs. Receipt gating and lifecycle copy changes look correct, but the feature missed contract coverage for restaurant thank-you alias canonicalization, so the review fails with one blocking issue.
